headline: Archer Aviation acquires former rival Wisk Aero in Boeing deal
summary: Boeing sells its air taxi startups to Archer Aviation in exchange for an ownership stake, marking a new chapter after a past trade secret lawsuit.
details: Electric aircraft company Archer Aviation has officially acquired Wisk Aero, its former rival, three years after settling a trade secret lawsuit. Boeing, Wisk's parent company, will receive a 16.5% ownership stake in Archer as part of the deal.

The acquisition includes Wisk Aero and two other Boeing subsidiaries: SkyGrid, a software company for digital airspace management, and drone maker Insitu. This move consolidates key players in the advanced air mobility sector.

The relationship between Archer and Wisk was previously contentious, with Wisk suing Archer in 2021 for alleged theft of confidential information. The lawsuit was settled two years later, leading to a collaboration where Archer agreed to make Wisk its exclusive provider of autonomous technology.

Wisk Aero originated from Kittyhawk, an electric aviation startup backed by Google co-founder Larry Page. After Kittyhawk shut down, Wisk, initially a joint venture with Boeing, became a fully-owned subsidiary of the aerospace giant.

Archer Aviation, founded in 2018, has been expanding its electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft program, including ventures into the defense sector. The company has secured significant funding and formed partnerships for defense applications.

Archer's all-electric Midnight aircraft recently completed a piloted round-trip flight, as the company prepares to launch operations later this year under the White House’s eVTOL Integration Pilot Program.

headline: Steam hardware data likely compromised in European shipping breach
summary: Valve warns European Steam hardware customers to watch for scam emails following a cyberattack on shipping partner CEVA Logistics.
details: Valve has alerted European Steam hardware customers that their personal data was likely exposed in a cyberattack targeting CEVA Logistics, a shipping partner. The breach occurred between July 29 and August 1, with Valve learning of the incident on August 7.

The compromised information includes customer names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, and order details. However, Valve has stated that sensitive data such as payment information, passwords, and Steam Guard codes were not accessed.

Affected users are not required to change their Steam passwords or account details. Valve is actively investigating the full scope of the breach with CEVA Logistics and has begun notifying data protection authorities in the affected European countries.

Valve is urging customers to be vigilant against potential phishing attempts. Scam emails, SMS messages, or phone calls may appear to be from Valve or a delivery company, using stolen order details to trick users into paying fees or divulging further information.
